newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U.N. tribunal prosecutor visits Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: U.N. tribunal prosecutor visits Bosnia.

text.p: The chief prosecutor for the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia held talks with Bosnian government officials on Monday as part of her tour of the Balkans.
Louise Arbour met Edhem Bicakcic, the prime minister of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation, and other cabinet members a day after arriving in the capital Sarajevo, officials said.

The Canadian judge, in her first visit to Bosnia since assuming her post last year, was due to hold talks with members of the newly-elected collective presidency as well as representatives from humanitarian organisations and the NATO-led peace force in Bosnia.
Arbour planned to meet Bosnian Serb leaders on Tuesday in their government seat of Pale, outside Sarajevo, home to indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic.
Bosnian Serb president Biljana Plavsic has ruled out extraditing Karadzic or the commander of the Serb army, Ratko Mladic, to face war crimes charges, saying their arrest could trigger civil unrest.
The tribunal has rejected Plavsic's argument and insisted that all those charged as suspects must be tried to ensure a lasting peace and reconciliation after four years of war in former Yugoslavia.
The U.N. tribunal has indicted more than 70 Serbs, Croats and Moslems for war crimes but only seven suspects have been extradited to The Hague to face trial.
